nodes.label: tsvector full-text search
nodes.rationale: Full-text search using tsvector column with GIN index is orders of magnitude faster than LIKE with wildcards; supports ranking via ts_rank and query operators & (AND), | (OR), :* (prefix).

nodes.label: JSONB GIN index
nodes.rationale: GIN indexes for JSONB containment queries (@>, ?, ?&, ?|); jsonb_ops supports all operators (larger index), jsonb_path_ops supports only @> (2-3x smaller index); expression indexes for specific key lookups.

nodes.label: Idle connection timeout
nodes.rationale: Configure idle_in_transaction_session_timeout and idle_session_timeout to automatically reclaim idle connections; pgbouncer pooler-level configuration via server_idle_timeout and client_idle_timeout; idle connections waste 1-3MB RAM each.

nodes.label: max_connections limit
nodes.rationale: Set max_connections based on available RAM (formula: RAM in MB / 5MB per connection minus reserved); work_mem * max_connections should not exceed 25% of RAM; excessive connections exhaust memory and degrade performance.

nodes.label: PgBouncer connection pooling
nodes.rationale: Postgres connections are expensive (1-3MB RAM each); use a pooler like PgBouncer between app and database; pool_size formula (CPU cores * 2) + spindle_count; transaction mode returns connection after each transaction, session mode holds for entire session.

nodes.label: Prepared statements with pooling
nodes.rationale: Prepared statements are tied to individual database connections; in transaction-mode pooling connections are shared causing conflicts; use unnamed prepared statements, deallocate after use, or session mode pooling to avoid 'prepared statement does not exist' errors.

nodes.label: Batch INSERT statements
nodes.rationale: Individual INSERT statements have high overhead (separate transaction and round trip each); batch multiple rows in single INSERT statement (~1000 rows per batch) or use COPY for fastest bulk loading.

nodes.label: N+1 query elimination
nodes.rationale: N+1 queries execute one query per item in a loop (101 round trips for 100 users); batch into single query using ANY(array) or JOIN to reduce to 1 round trip.

nodes.label: Connection Management rule category
nodes.rationale: Section 2 of 8 rule categories with prefix 'conn-', CRITICAL impact; covers connection pooling, limits, and serverless strategies, critical for high concurrency or serverless deployments.

nodes.label: Data Access Patterns rule category
nodes.rationale: Section 6 of 8 rule categories with prefix 'data-', MEDIUM impact; covers N+1 query elimination, batch operations, cursor-based pagination, and efficient data fetching.

nodes.label: Composite Index
nodes.rationale: A composite index on multiple columns is more efficient than separate single-column indexes for multi-column queries. Column order matters: place equality columns first, range columns last, following the leftmost prefix rule.

nodes.label: Covering Index (INCLUDE)
nodes.rationale: Covering indexes include all columns needed by a query via INCLUDE, enabling index-only scans that skip table heap fetches entirely.

nodes.label: Index Type Selection
nodes.rationale: Different index types excel at different query patterns: B-tree for equality/range, GIN for arrays/JSONB/full-text, GiST for geometric/range/KNN, BRIN for large time-series, Hash for equality-only lookups.

nodes.label: Missing Index / Sequential Scan
nodes.rationale: Queries filtering or joining on unindexed columns cause full table scans that become exponentially slower as tables grow; add indexes on WHERE and JOIN columns, especially the foreign key side.

nodes.label: Partial Index
nodes.rationale: Partial indexes only include rows matching a WHERE condition, making them smaller and faster for queries that consistently filter on the same condition (e.g., active users, pending orders, non-null values).

nodes.label: Table Constraint
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL does not support ADD CONSTRAINT IF NOT EXISTS; use DO blocks checking pg_constraint for idempotent constraint creation. contype values: p primary key, f foreign key, u unique, c check.

nodes.label: Data Type Selection
nodes.rationale: Use bigint not int for IDs, text not varchar(n), timestamptz not timestamp, numeric not float for money, and text with check constraint or enum type for enums; reduces storage and improves comparison performance.

nodes.label: Foreign Key Index
nodes.rationale: Postgres does not automatically index foreign key columns; missing indexes cause slow JOINs and ON DELETE CASCADE operations requiring full table scans. Always index the FK (referencing) column.

nodes.label: Primary Key Strategy
nodes.rationale: Primary key choice affects insert performance, index size, and replication efficiency. Prefer bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY for single databases; UUIDv7 (pg_uuidv7) or time-prefixed IDs for distributed systems; avoid random UUIDv4 on large tables due to index fragmentation.

nodes.label: Principle of Least Privilege
nodes.rationale: Grant only the minimum permissions required; never use superuser for application queries. Create nologin roles with specific grants (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE on named tables, sequence usage), revoke default public access, and let login roles inherit via role membership.

nodes.label: Row Level Security (RLS)
nodes.rationale: RLS enforces data access at the database level so users only see their own data. Enable RLS on tables, create policies using current_setting or auth.uid(), force RLS for table owners, and set user context via session variables.
